No, no, never. Honestly, before all this started happening recently, I never dealt with anything like that. I mean, I've always been a pretty regular guy, you know? Just went to high school, got my diploma, started working my way up in the wholesale business. I never had any weird stuff going on in my head. 

I remember back when I first started as a junior buyer—this was a couple years ago, way before any of this current mess—I was just focused on learning the ropes, figuring out how the purchase orders worked, getting to know the vendors. My mood was always just... normal. I'd go to work, do my hours, go home, watch some TV, hang out. I never heard anyone talking to me when I was alone in the stockroom back then. The stockroom was just quiet, you know? Just me and the boxes. 

And the whole tracking thing? Not even a blip on my radar back then. I used to just punch in my buys on the terminal, log off, and not give it a second thought. I never once worried that the senior guys or anyone else was trying to steal my angles or put keyloggers on my system. I just trusted the process. It's so crazy to think about how different it was. I was just a regular 22-year-old trying to make a living. So, yeah, before this whole recent situation with the wild energy and then the voices and the tracking... no, I never experienced anything like that when I was just feeling normal. It's all completely new, and honestly, it's pretty terrifying when you compare it to how quiet my life used to be.

turns.doctor_question: At any point, did the voice start when your mood was completely normal, before any high or irritable period began?
turns.patient_response:
Well, let me think back... it's a little hard to untangle it all sometimes, you know? Because everything just kind of bleeds together when you're in the middle of it. But if I really sit down and trace it back... no, I don't think the voice or the tracking stuff started before the high energy kicked in. 

But, I mean, the whole thing—the voice in the stockroom, the absolute certainty that people are logging my keystrokes on the terminal, all of those suspicious beliefs—they've been going on for roughly ten months now. Ten whole months of this. It started around the end of last year, maybe? Yeah, about ten months. And it's just been this constant thing ever since, whether I'm bouncing off the walls and feeling like I own the wholesale market, or whether I'm in that calm, normal stretch like we were just talking about. 

It's just wild to think it's been almost a year of dealing with this. Ten months of looking over my shoulder at the terminal, ten months of dreading going into the stockroom because I know I'm going to hear it. It feels like a lifetime, honestly, but yeah, the timeline is right around ten months for all the suspicious stuff and the voice. But as for it starting *before* I ever got that initial crazy rush of energy and irritability? No, I'm pretty sure the super high energy kind of kicked the door open for everything else, and then the voice and the tracking fears just moved in and stayed for the last ten months.

turns.doctor_question: Altogether, have the voice and the feeling that people were plotting against you lasted for at least one full month?
turns.patient_response:
Oh, definitely. Like I was just saying a minute ago, it's been way, way longer than a month. I mean, honestly, I wish it had only been a month! A month I could probably handle, you know? Like, you can grit your teeth and get through a bad four weeks at the wholesale market. Like when the holiday shipments get backed up or a major vendor screws up a purchase order, you just put your head down and push through it for a month. 

But this isn't just a bad month. Like I mentioned, the suspicious beliefs and the voice have been happening for roughly ten months now. Ten whole months. When you really sit down and think about how many days that actually is... how many times I've had to walk into that stockroom to check inventory and just brace myself, waiting to hear it. Or how many times I've sat at my terminal, totally convinced someone is logging my keystrokes to steal my purchase angles and sabotage my numbers. It's exhausting just talking about it. Ten months of looking over my shoulder every single shift, trying to figure out who's plotting against me while I'm just trying to do my job. 

So, yeah, if you're asking if it's been at least one full month, the answer is a massive yes. It's basically been almost a year of my life just swallowed up by this stuff, day in and day out, whether my mood is totally fine or I'm bouncing off the walls. Ten months of it.

turns.doctor_question: Have you had at least two weeks when you were hearing the voice while your mood felt completely normal?
turns.patient_response:
Yeah, yeah I have. Actually, it's funny you ask about that specific timeframe, because I was just thinking about this stretch... I guess it was a little while back, maybe a couple months ago? I remember it really clearly because, for a second there, I thought maybe I was getting better, or at least getting back to my old self. My energy had finally leveled out. I wasn't waking up at 3 AM with a million ideas for new vendor contracts, and I wasn't talking a mile a minute to the senior buyers. I was actually sleeping through the night, getting a solid seven or eight hours, which was huge for me. I felt... calm. Just normal, regular calm. Not like I was running the whole wholesale market single-handedly, just going in, doing my job, grabbing lunch at the deli across the street, coming back. 

But the thing is, even though my mood was totally fine, completely baseline, the other stuff didn't stop. Not at all. For that whole stretch—it was definitely a few weeks, maybe three or four weeks of just feeling totally regular mood-wise—I was still absolutely convinced that they were tracking my buys on the terminal. I'd sit there, feeling totally calm, but still knowing, just knowing, that someone had a keylogger on my system, watching every purchase order I punched in. And the voice in the stockroom? Still there. I'd go back there to check on a shipment of overstock, feeling completely rested and normal, and I'd still hear it. Just as clear as day. 

It was almost more disturbing that way, honestly. When you're all keyed up and your thoughts are racing, the weird stuff almost fits the vibe, you know? But when you're just sitting there, sipping a coffee, feeling totally fine, and you still hear someone talking to you in an empty room, or you're still terrified to type on your own keyboard... it really messes with your head. So, yeah, there was definitely a period of a few weeks where my mood was totally normal, but the tracking fears and the voice just kept right on going. It didn't take a break just because my energy did.

turns.doctor_question: During the past year, have you ever had two weeks in a row when you felt depressed most of the day nearly every day?
turns.patient_response:
Depressed? Like, really down for two weeks straight? No, I don't think so. Not for two weeks in a row, anyway. I mean, sure, I get bummed out sometimes, who doesn't? Especially in wholesale, it can be a real grind, you know? You're constantly dealing with vendors who promise one thing and deliver another, or the logistics get messed up, and you're just sitting there at your desk feeling like you're banging your head against a brick wall. And honestly, dealing with all the tracking stuff... the keylogger on my terminal, the feeling that someone is always watching my purchase orders... that can really drag a guy down. It gets exhausting, it really does. 

There are definitely days where I just feel totally wiped out by it all, where I just want to put my head down on the desk and not talk to anyone. But it's never been like, two solid weeks of just feeling depressed all day, every day. It's more like I'll have a bad day or two where I'm just fed up and tired, but then the energy comes back. Usually, the energy comes back pretty strong, actually. I'll go from feeling totally drained to suddenly realizing I need to overhaul the entire inventory system right this second, and I'll be up for three days straight trying to make it happen. 

So, yeah, it's more of a roller coaster. I don't really get stuck down in the dumps for weeks on end. It's more like these quick dips, mostly just because I'm so burnt out from everything else going on, and then I'm right back up again, running a million miles a minute. So no, not two weeks of just being depressed. It just doesn't stay that way for that long.
